text:
anita: thinking out loud — can we build a probe-less canary rollback signal based on model output entropy/divergence instead of running expensive E2E probes?

mike: interesting, do you mean entropy of logits or token distribution? how cheap is it to compute at router time?

anita: both. idea: compute token-level entropy + KL to a rolling baseline per route. aggregate over a short window (5-10 requests) and surface a single divergence metric. cheap because we can sample topk or use cached summary stats instead of full probes.

olga: two quick flags: 1) exposing logits/entropy crosses a privacy/telemetry boundary for hosted -> who stores this? 2) runtime placement: router vs model runtime — adding work to router might hurt p99.

mike: agree on runtime placement concern. maybe have the model runtime emit a compact summary metric (e.g., mean entropy, sample hash) rather than raw logits, then router/policy sees only the summary.

anita: exactly — runtime emits summaries to the metrics bus. policy service subscribes and makes binary decisions (allow/fallback). sample config sketch:

```json
{"policy": "entropy_kl_guard", "window_sec": 30, "min_samples": 20, "kl_threshold": 0.12, "hysteresis_windows": 3, "fallback": "variant:small-quantized"}
```

sre-jen: how do we avoid false positives from sudden prompt distribution shifts (e.g., an app experiment that changes prompt patterns)? we need tenant-level baselines and cooldown.

anita: agreed. proposed guards: tenant-scoped baselines, require N consecutive windows above threshold, and require concurrent signal from at least one other orthogonal metric (latency or hallucination evals) before auto-fallback. fallback can be degrade-to-cache or to a cheaper model variant.

olga: ownership note — metric-store should be infra-owned (long retention). policy-service reads baselines and writes decisions. router only asks policy-service for a decision per route/request and enforces it. that keeps router thin.

mike: that boundary sounds right: runtime -> metric-store (summaries); policy-service -> decision; router -> enforcement. also need an operator override in Console to pause auto-fallbacks per-customer.

deploy-bot: deploy note: experiment/entropy-canary featureflag enabled on staging (canary=2%) :rocket:

sre-jen: ops safety checklist: add manual rollback button, circuit-breaker counter, alert on aggregate KL spikes, and a dry-run mode where policy only logs decisions for 24h.

anita: next steps I propose: a short RFC that (1) defines summary schema, (2) maps runtime->metric-store interfaces, (3) policy decision contract, (4) console controls + audit logs. then a small prototype in Dedicated with feature-flagged routing. thoughts? :thumbsup:

mike: +1. will volunteer to help perf test the summary emission path.

olga: +1 from infra side, will scope retention/cost impact.

sre-jen: +1 on dry-run first. want to see false positive stats before enabling auto-fallback.

anita: cool — I'll draft RFC and ping this thread when ready. Thanks all!
